text.p: Drug development group Cortecs International Ltd said on Monday that it had signed a worldwide licensing agreement for diagnosing tuberculosis with Canadian group Inflazyme Pharmaceuticals Ltd.
Cortecs said under the agreement, the companies would develop the ELISA test and rapid point of care tests for the diagnosis of tuberculosis.

It said the agreement involves equity investment, milestone payments and royalties. The firms plan to use their existing technologies and expertise to develop and commercialise a series of diagnostic products, using whole blood, plasma, serum or saliva, suitable to assist in rapid diagnosis of tuberculosis.
It said more than 1.7 billion people worldwide or one third of the world's population have dormant tuberculosis infections.
"Tuberculosis remains a global disease and simple methods of diagnosis which can be carried out without additional apparatus are needed to improve detection and management programmes," Cortecs said.

Cortecs said it hopes that through the development of both ELISA and Rapid Point of Care tests it will be able to assist in identifying patients and controlling the spread of tuberculosis through communities around the world.
Cortecs is listed in Australia, United Kingdom and the United States. At 3.50 p.m. (0450 GMT), Cortecs shares were four cents lower at A$3.80.
